messages:
maya: heads-up — nightly eval flagged a weird regression on bring-up for quant-ggml-2.1. seems tied to the promptbank merge from feature/prompt-curation earlier today :thinking_face:
jonathan: ugh. which regression metric? rouge/acc or our custom instruction-follow fidelity? :eyes:
maya: fidelity drops on a small subset of instruction prompts. CI shows a canary fallback to baseline model during the run. suspect the harness fed the wrong prompt fixtures after the merge.
eva: i pulled the run logs — eval-runner printed: 'Loaded promptset: promptbank:v2.7 (conflict-resolved)' then later 'Using fallback fixtures: promptbank:v2.5' — that's a red flag.
ci-bot: Pipeline #512 failed: eval-harness/regressions detected. See: https://ci.redwood/512 -- failing tests: fidelity-regress, promptset-consistency.
ranjit: possible cause: merge resolved some duplicate prompt_ids by renaming them, but runner maps ids -> fixtures with cache keys that include the commit hash. if the mapping table didn't get updated, fallback to older mapping happens.
kevin: i also saw a git conflict marker buried in promptbank/index.yaml during the merge. snippet:
```
<<<<<<< HEAD
- prompt_id: pb_093
  text: "Summarize the article in one sentence."
=======
- prompt_id: pb_093_v2
  text: "Summarize this article in a single sentence, include tone."
>>>>>>> feature/prompt-curation
```
maya: exact. the merge bot auto-resolved by keeping both entries but the index loader strips suffixes, producing id collisions. That caused the harness to de-dupe and select older fixture entries.
jonathan: quick triage: 1) freeze merges to promptbank, 2) run the repair script to normalise prompt_ids and bump the promptset version, 3) re-run the failing canary with forced promptset=explicit commit.
eva: small script idea to detect these conflicts in CI — if index.yaml contains both pb_093 and pb_093_v2 within 3 lines flag as merge residue. i can open a PR.
ranjit: also need a fix in the eval runner: when fallback occurs, emit a structured warning with the promptset ids used and the mapping commit. right now it logs free text which CI doesn't parse.
kevin: agreed. i'll add a gating test in eval CI that asserts index.yaml is id-canonical (regex: ^prompt_id: pb_[0-9]{3}(_v[0-9]+)?$ is allowed but then ensure downstream mapping resolves to an exact canonical id).
ci-bot: Note: New job suggestion — promptbank-lint will run on PRs touching /data/promptbank/**.
maya: one more wrinkle — quantized bring-up uses synthetic augmentations to create negative prompts. when prompt ids shift, synthetic fixture generation can sample holdout prompts that shouldn't be in validation. that explains leakage pattern we saw earlier this week.
jonathan: re: leakage — we should add a guard: synthetic generator must assert no overlap with validation prompt fingerprint set (sha256). quick patch idea: store a fingerprint list per promptset commit and reject generators that sample from any fingerprint present.
eva: i'll prototype fingerprint compare util today. should be cheap.
ranjit: for the short term, can we re-run the failed canary with PROMPTSET=commit/abc123 (pre-merge) and QUANT_PROFILE=debug so we can isolate model vs prompt differences?
kevin: launching that now. tagging @eng-oncall if it starts hitting infra quotas.
ci-bot: Rerun requested: Pipeline #512. New run id #513 queued.
maya: thanks — if #513 passes we know the merge introduced the issue. if it still fails, we dig into quant changes. either way, we need: promptbank lint in CI, runner fallback to be structured, and synthetic-generator fingerprint checks. I'll open a tracking ticket.
jonathan: can you add the ticket link when you create it? i'll pick up the runner parsing fix.
maya: will do. ticket: https://tracker.redwood/issue/ML-2381 — "promptbank merge residues causing CI fallback and leakage"
eva: jotting down action items: PR for promptbank-lint, deploy fingerprint util, eval-runner structured warnings, repair script for current promptset.
kevin: one more low-level note — the caching layer (prompt-mapper cache) TTL is 24h. if someone merges and reverts within that window, the runner might still see stale mappings. consider invalidating cache on promptset update.
ranjit: or include promptset commit hash in cache key so update always invalidates.
maya: nice. i'll include that in the ticket. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin: will follow up on infra and queue the canary results here.
ci-bot: Pipeline #513 completed: status=success. No regressions detected.
maya: OK that confirms the merge caused the problem. closing the loop after PRs land.
jonathan: thanks — long-term we should add a small end-to-end smoke in PR checklist that boots eval-runner against a stable snapshot before merging prompt changes. fast and cheap.
maya: agreed. closing thread after PR reviews.
